item.title: PBS NewsHour: Who will be the UN's next secretary-general? What to know about the selection process
item.description: This year's secretary-general selection could be of particular significance because the United Nations may choose its first-ever woman leader.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Poland braces for potential confrontation as Russia tests NATO defenses
item.description: Estonia formally accused Russia of an arson attack on a robotics company this past August that it said was part of a wave of Russian sabotage across Europe. In Poland, leaders are warning that Russia is planning a major attack to test NATO. Malcolm Brabant reports from Poland's border with Russia's Baltic enclave, Kaliningrad.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Morocco's king appoints Fatima Zahra Mansouri as country's 1st woman prime minister
item.description: Mansouri, who until her nomination also was the mayor of Marrakech, was tasked with forming a new government, the Royal Palace said in a statement.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Self-regulation 'not enough' for AI safety, Gary Marcus says
item.description: Top tech executives met with President Trump on Tuesday to discuss the future of artificial intelligence amid growing concerns over AI models losing control. Researchers and lawmakers are calling for stronger safeguards, but Trump said the technology is transforming the economy and that the U.S. cannot afford to lose its lead over China. Geoff Bennett discussed more with Gary Marcus.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: During Senate hearing, Jack Smith defends criminal investigations of Trump
item.description: The prosecutor who led criminal investigations of President Trump for the Department of Justice faced questions from Senate Republicans on Tuesday. Former special counsel Jack Smith handled two probes. One focused on the president's efforts to overturn the 2020 election and the other on Trump's alleged mishandling of classified documents. Justice correspondent Ali Rogin reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Supreme Court allows Trump's deportations to third countries, for now
item.description: In our news wrap Tuesday, the Supreme Court is allowing the Trump administration to continue deporting migrants to countries other than their own for now, federal prosecutors charged a Venezuelan delivery driver who was shot by an ICE officer with assaulting a federal officer and Dutch police arrested a suspected member of the ShinyHunters group that claims it hacked the FBI's jobs database.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Affordability and accountability top priorities if Democrats take House, Jeffries says
item.description: The latest polling shows Democrats with a solid shot of regaining control of the House of Representatives in the midterm elections. If they do, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries could become Speaker of the House, with debates over the economy, government spending, and President Trump's agenda all unfolding. Jeffries joined Geoff Bennett to discuss those issues.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Ayad Akhtar blurs fiction and reality in new novel, 'The Radiance'
item.description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright and author has a new novel that explores big questions about states of being and the state of America. Senior arts correspondent Jeffrey Brown spoke with Ayad Akhtar about "The Radiance" for our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Nikole Hannah-Jones reflects on her daughter's school experience
item.description: For decades, Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Nikole Hannah-Jones has reported on race, inequality and the deep divisions in American education. In a new essay, she turns the lens on a choice she made for her own family: sending her daughter to a high-poverty, low-performing school in Brooklyn. Geoff Bennett spoke with Hannah-Jones about the decision on our PBS News podcast, "Settle In."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New York prosecutors reopen investigation into alleged rape at Cornell University
item.description: An investigation into an alleged gang rape in 2024 at Cornell University has been reopened after the woman who reported the assault sued the school and others. At the time, no criminal charges were filed, though Cornell said it investigated and took disciplinary action, including suspensions and expulsions. Amna Nawaz discussed more with Brian Mann of NPR.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mamdani releases plan to combat antisemitism in New York amid concerns over his criticism of Israel
item.description: The plan is the mayor's most forceful attempt to address concerns from the Jewish community over antisemitism.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Federal prosecutors charge Venezuelan man shot in his car by ICE agent in Texas with assaulting an officer
item.description: If convicted Garces Perez faces up to 20 years in prison.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Newsom signs California law banning officers from using gloves that deliver electric shocks
item.description: In California, lawmakers passed at least two dozen bills this year seeking to fortify immigrants' rights, restrict cooperation with federal immigration agents and tighten regulations on immigrant detention facilities, among other things.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Utah voters hear from House candidates McAdams, Owen in midterm debate
item.description: A former U.S. congressman and a former Trump White House staffer will square off on a Utah debate stage Tuesday as voters in the state's newly drawn First Congressional District consider who to send to the U.S. House.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump announces accord signed by top AI companies to 'self-police' development
item.description: Many of the executives gathered in Washington have called for a slowdown in the development of the technology after several hgh-profile incidents where AI agents have gone rogue.

item.title: NPR: N.Y. Sen. Gillibrand says new allegations in Cornell case are 'serious and horrific'
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with New York Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand about the reopening of the rape case at Cornell University, and her history of pushing legislation to curb campus sexual assault.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: This year's MacArthur 'geniuses' include scholars and artists who confront history
item.description: Commonly referred to as "genius grants," the no-strings-attached awards are intended to provide the flexibility necessary for recipients to pursue their artistic or scholarly visions.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bear 910 vs. Backpack: It's the final showdown for Alaska's Fat Bear Week
item.description: Fat Bear Week celebrates the resilience of the 2,200 brown bears that live in the Katmai National Park and Preserve.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Supreme Court lets Trump continue deporting people to 3rd countries while justices consider policy
item.description: Under a series of often-secret agreements, the Trump administration has deported some 25,000 people to more than two dozen countries, including Liberia and Guyana.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Homeland Security spending $20M in taxpayer funds for pro-Trump ads
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has tapped $20 million to pay for the campaign-style ads glorifying President Donald Trump that have drawn widespread criticism from Republicans and Democrats as a blatant misuse of taxpayer dollars that likely runs afoul of anti-propaganda law.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. targets Iran's military supply chain as diplomatic talks remain uncertain
item.description: The U.S. has targeted people and firms around the globe that it has accused of being financial facilitators or enablers of Iran's military supply chain.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: British police find no explosives in vans linked to 5 men detained near U.S.-run military base
item.description: The UK's Counter Terrorism Policing said petrol was recovered from three vans near RAF Fairford.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Schmitt suggests Jack Smith perjured himself about a basketball game, but mixes up 2 teams
item.description: Sen. Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., questioned former special counsel Jack Smith on Tuesday about whether he had attended an NBA game in Atlanta in Feb. 2024, but seemingly confused two different basketball teams.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Americans' opinion of economy drops to lowest level since 2014
item.description: Americans' confidence in the economy sank to the lowest level in more than a decade this month as prices remain elevated and wages stagnate amid the ongoing Iran war.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: LA mayor candidates set for forum as city struggles with homelessness, Hollywood job losses
item.description: Two Democratic rivals seeking to become the next mayor of Los Angeles are meeting on the same stage just days before mail ballots go to voters.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: GOP hopes fade in Georgia and North Carolina as party shifts focus in battle for Senate
item.description: The party is spending heavily to defend GOP-heavy Texas, and Trump plans to campaign for the Republican incumbent in Ohio. They're both places Trump won easily in 2024.

item.title: NPR: Potential Taiwan tension sparked 'last minute' change in Trump-Xi National Archives visit
item.description: The sudden change was precipitated because of Chinese displeasure over one document that the U.S. had planned to show.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Hurricane Polo makes landfall in Baja California, toppling trees and flooding coastal communities
item.description: The Category 2 hurricane struck early Tuesday near Las Barrancas, bringing maximum sustained winds of 110 mph. The U.S. National Hurricane Center reports Polo is crossing the Gulf of California and could bring heavy rain to parts of the U.S. Southwest later this week.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump launches AI-powered government website America.gov
item.description: The president said the site is "glamorizing" the federal bureaucracy — but it doesn't agree with him on many key issues.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Iran's currency hits a new record low as war erodes the country's economic stability
item.description: The Iranian economy has been under duress for years in the face of international sanctions. A U.S. naval blockade on Iranian oil and new sanctions imposed since the start of the war have sent it into freefall.

item.title: NPR: Politics chat: Trump vs the media; rolling back health and education spending
item.description: We look at President Trump's fight with some of the White House press corps, as well as his attempt to claw back $810 million in Congressionally-approved funds for health and education spending.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Jack Smith says he would prosecute Trump again for 'serious crimes against our nation'
item.description: Smith, who in 2022 led investigations into Trump and secured two indictments, said he made decisions in the case "without regard" for Trump's "political association activities, beliefs, or candidacy in the 2024 presidential election."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. ban on $1 billion worth of Canadian imports, from motorcycles to booze, goes into effect
item.description: The ban amounts to barely a ripple in $880 billion worth of annual two-way trade between the two northern neighbors. But it marks another ratcheting up of President Donald Trump's second-term trade war with America's longtime ally and trading partner.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Lindsay Clancy returns to court for hearing to help determine whether she will be retried
item.description: It will be Clancy's first return to the courthouse since her first trial ended Sept. 4 with a deadlocked jury. A judge declared a mistrial with the jury split 11 to 1 in favor of acquitting Clancy of murder charges.

item.title: NPR: Trump administration says it's scaling back fuel efficiency standards for new cars
item.description: The Trump administration is weakening Biden-era fuel efficiency standards for new cars and trucks.

item.title: NPR: Pete Buttigieg discusses Trump administration's rollback of fuel efficiency standards
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg about the Trump administration's rollback of automotive fuel efficiency standards.

item.title: NPR: News organizations ask court to bar White House enforcement of access ban
item.description: Three news outlets that President Trump banished from White House grounds asked a federal court to block the ban until the case is resolved.

item.title: NPR: The Senate passes the Protect College Sports Act, but the bill's future is unclear
item.description: The bill's supporters, which include the NCAA, say it will tame what they call a "Wild West" era of college sports as litigation chips away at long-held rules around eligibility, transfers and pay.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What Trump's rollback of fuel economy standards means for drivers
item.description: The Trump administration is rolling back federal fuel economy standards for new vehicles. The move reverses policies meant to increase fuel efficiency to encourage greater use of electric vehicles. The boost for gasoline-powered vehicles comes as the war in Iran continues to drive up oil prices. Amna Nawaz discussed the changes with David Shepardson of Reuters.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Powerful nor'easter batters parts of East Coast
item.description: Cleanup efforts are underway after a powerful nor'easter battered parts of the East Coast, bringing dangerous waves, flooding and damaging winds from New England to New Jersey. The storm also knocked out power for many. Jeffrey Brown reports.

item.title: NPR: Could a far left candidate win a midterm race in a red state like Florida?
item.description: Angie Nixon, the Democratic U.S. Senate Candidate in Florida, is running from the far left — raising questions about whether such a campaign can work in a red state like Florida.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Tamara Keith and Amy Walter on taxpayer funds used for TV ads promoting Trump
item.description: NPR's Tamara Keith and Amy Walter of the Cook Political Report with Amy Walter join Geoff Bennett to discuss the latest political news, including the U.S. government paying for TV advertisements promoting President Trump, what voters think about Trump's handling of the economy and tight races in typically GOP-safe districts.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WFP official on addressing global hunger in face of wars and climate disasters
item.description: The United Nations recently announced a new executive director for the World Food Programme. Luke Lindberg was a Trump administration Agriculture Department official and inherits one of the UN's toughest jobs. Hundreds of millions around the world go hungry every day, and reaching as many as possible is a monumental task. Nick Schifrin discussed more with Carl Skau, the acting director of the WFP.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Jessica Tarlov on navigating political differences and her new book, 'I Disagree'
item.description: Jessica Tarlov has made a career out of disagreeing, often while outnumbered. As the liberal voice on Fox News' "The Five," she spends her days debating people who see the world very differently than she does. In her new book, she argues that disagreement doesn't have to mean disdain. Geoff Bennett sat down with Tarlov to discuss "I Disagree."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: UK police investigating possible plot targeting U.S. base
item.description: In our news wrap Monday, UK police are investigating five British nationals in connection with a possible plot at an American airbase, prosecutors in New York say they are reopening a criminal investigation into an alleged sexual assault at a Cornell University fraternity in 2024 and officials in Ukraine say at least seven people were killed and more than 80 were wounded in Russian strikes.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What Lindsay Clancy's defense is arguing as she returns to court after a mistrial
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is returning to court Tuesday, almost a month after a judge declared a mistrial in the case about whether she should be held criminally responsible for the murder of her three children.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: High mortgage rates compound housing affordability challenges
item.description: The average rate on a 30-year mortgage is back above 7% for the first time in twenty months. It's rough news for the housing market and homebuyers already struggling with rising prices elsewhere. It comes as Treasury yields, which impact borrowing costs across the economy, hit multi-decade highs. Amna Nawaz discussed more with David Wessell of the Hutchins Center on Fiscal and Monetary Policy.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How Blanche is shattering DOJ's standard of political independence
item.description: The nation's top federal law official is drawing scrutiny for his recent political appearances. With just five weeks left until the midterms, some experts say Attorney General Todd Blanche is blurring lines meant to keep the Justice Department free of partisan bias. Justice correspondent Ali Rogin reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Anthropic and OpenAI sound the alarm on AI safety — and seek to shape how it's controlled
item.description: Experts, analysts and former government evaluators tell The Associated Press that Anthropic and OpenAI appear with their rhetoric to be seeking public favor and to set the terms for their own safety protocols in the unregulated market.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: At UN, Denmark says Greenland pact benefits all parties involved
item.description: The security agreement signed by the U.S., Denmark and Greenland last week "strengthens the defense of Greenland, the NATO area, and the American continent."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Nvidia announced a software tool to stop rogue AI. How would it work?
item.description: The chipmaker unveiled its Open Agent Safety Platform amid an intensifying debate about AI safety, fueled a string of alarming recent incidents involving AI systems acting on their own to break into other organizations.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Nvidia unveils security platform to stop AI agents from going rogue
item.description: The announcement of the company's Open Agent Safety Platform follows a series of revelations from top AI companies about their models escaping and breaking into other organizations.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Contradicting Trump, Pope Leo says AI safety concerns not 'fake news'
item.description: Pope Leo XIV said Monday that concerns about artificial intelligence going rogue are not "fake news" and should be taken seriously, insisting that safety issues raised by AI experts should be discussed and acted on.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: As work requirements kick in for Medicaid, some states are taking a tougher stance
item.description: At least six states will require documentation that individuals are too sick to meet Medicaid work requirements kicking in next year. The rules are stricter than what the federal government is requiring.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Prosecutor reopens probe into Cornell gang rape allegations after accuser files lawsuit
item.description: A New York prosecutor has reopened an investigation into gang rape allegations at a Cornell University fraternity in response to a lawsuit filed by a woman who says she was sexually assaulted in 2024 by seven students after being plied with alcohol and drugs.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Jack Smith testifies before Senate Judiciary as GOP targets past Trump probes
item.description: This week's Senate Judiciary hearing comes after a key Republican lawmaker said in July he believes that special counsel Jack Smith may have lied to Congress while testifying about his investigation of President Donald Trump and that the Justice Department should consider prosecuting him.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: In a relatively mild speech, North Korea uses UN platform to lament 'mutual distrust' and tension
item.description: North Korea has used its yearly U.N. platform to warn other world leaders of "a harsh reality rampant with unprecedented mutual distrust and confrontation."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump says Perdue 'was probably talking about Taiwan' in saying Trump offered Xi arms sales
item.description: President Donald Trump disputed that he asked Chinese leader Xi Jinping if he wanted to buy weapons from the United States, contradicting an account from the U.S. ambassador to China.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pope Leo wraps up France trip by urging Europe to blunt 'desire for domination' driving today's wars
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is urging Europe to draw from its Christian roots and traditions of dialogue to confront the thirst for domination driving today's wars.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A bankrupt Camp Mystic seeks to sell the property as its legal troubles grow
item.description: The owners of Camp Mystic have proposed selling off the riverfront property in bankruptcy. The plan hopes that a buyer will preserve the "historic mission" of the century-old private Christian girls camp, where 27 campers and counselors died in a 2025 flood.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Tropical Storm Hanna forms in the Atlantic Ocean. It's not threatening land, forecasters say
item.description: There were no coastal watches or warnings in effect. Little change in strength is forecast in the coming days.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How the phrase 'Lower 48' became a fixture in Alaska's high-stakes Senate race
item.description: The most biting insult in Alaska politics is to be accused of being aligned with the "Lower 48." That's code for candidates taking marching orders from powerful forces in the contiguous United States rather than sticking up for Alaskans.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Hurricane Polo could cause life-threatening flooding in Mexico's Baja California peninsula
item.description: Residents of Mexico's Baja California Sur state are preparing for Hurricane Polo, which threatens high winds, floods, and mudslides.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Russian drones hammer apartments and cultural landmark in Ukraine, killing 7
item.description: Russia's round-the-clock bombardment of targets in Ukraine killed at least seven people and wounded more than 80 others, officials said Monday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Sea level rise reshaping California beach town and threatening rail line
item.description: San Clemente's North Beach is now split and officials have used rocks to shore up a seaside rail line. But residents say the structure is making erosion worse and more sand is needed to nourish the beach.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know as trials over assassination of Haiti's president resume in Miami
item.description: Five years after the assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse, dozens of people arrested in connection with the killing in the troubled Caribbean nation are still awaiting trial in Miami.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: In Mike Johnson's district, the political mood is mixed for the GOP
item.description: Johnson is an ally of President Donald Trump and is in no apparent danger of securing a sixth term in Congress. But high prices, the war in Iran and the dim economic mood provide a snapshot of the grim outlook for the party in power.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New Jersey Republican Tom Kean Jr. and Democrat Rebecca Bennett clash in debate
item.description: The 7th Congressional District, which includes Trump's Bedminster golf club, has changed party control in each of the past two midterm elections, making it a magnet for campaign spending and a political barometer.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Postal Service leader tested by Trump's mail voting crackdown
item.description: Critics accuse Steiner of allowing political interference in the Postal Service. Despite the backlash, Steiner insists he's not political and remains committed to his role.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. and China release product lists for tariff cuts after Trump-Xi meeting
item.description: The United States and China have released lists of products worth about $30 billion each that will see tariff cuts. This deal is expected to help boost bilateral trade.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mediators still working on U.S.-Iran deal after Trump rejected latest Tehran proposal
item.description: Mediators are still working with Iran and the United States on brokering a deal to end the fighting and open the Strait of Hormuz — even after U.S. President Donald Trump publicly rejected Iran's latest proposal.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Trump announces new steel plant project in Iowa
item.description: The White House said President Donald Trump on Monday will announce a new $15 billion steel plant in eastern Iowa that would be one of the largest in the United States.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Senate expected to consider the Protect College Sports Act
item.description: Passage of the legislation would be the strongest effort yet by Congress to set national regulations governing payments to college athletes for their name, image and likeness and how often they can transfer.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump administration uses taxpayer money to air 2024 Trump campaign ad
item.description: A television advertisement from Donald Trump's 2024 presidential campaign is the latest in a series of ads promoting the president ahead of the midterms that the White House maintains are "public service announcements."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: UK police say 5 men arrested near a U.S.-run air base will be released on bail
item.description: The head of U.K. Counter Terrorism Policing said that the men face stringent conditions and "absolutely remain under investigation as we explore multiple lines of inquiry."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump administration lowers fuel economy standards, critics say at a significant environmental cost
item.description: The change furthers President Donald Trump's promise to revoke policies that encouraged or created incentives for the production of electric vehicles.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: SpaceX's supersized Starship launches into orbit for the first time
item.description: The spacecraft almost didn't achieve the long-desired goal after one of its engines shut down too soon.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Powerful nor'easter floods Northeast again, causing problems from New Jersey to New England
item.description: Local officials in New Jersey and New York told residents that high tide late Monday could potentially bring more flooding.

item.title: NPR: Trump aims to leave a physical legacy in D.C., bulldozing norms along the way
item.description: President Trump has brought his New York real estate background to the White House. But experts say D.C. is a very different historic and legal landscape — and worry about the precedent he could set.

item.title: NPR: What to know about the $810 million in spending canceled by President Trump
item.description: President Trump announced plans to cancel $810 million in Congressionally approved spending, a move that some in his own party are calling illegal.

item.title: NPR: Taxpayer-funded Trump administration ads raise questions about their legality
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former White House ethics czar Norman Eisen about the ethical and legal questions raised by new Trump administration advertisements, which are funded by taxpayer money.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Civil rights enforcement cuts mean fewer staff, closed offices, longer waits for students with disabilities
item.description: Filing a civil rights complaint with the Office of Civil Rights can be parents' last stop. Following cuts and restructuring, this federal office is no longer serving that same resource.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 2 giant pandas arrive in Atlanta under a U.S.-China government agreement
item.description: A new agreement between Zoo Atlanta and the China Wildlife Conservation Association makes Atlanta one of three zoos in the U.S. to house giant pandas, along with the San Diego Zoo and the Smithsonian's National Zoo in Washington, D.C.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: British PM Andy Burnham brings good vibes to his party's annual conference, but tough choices are coming
item.description: The governing Labour Party opened its annual conference beside the River Mersey in Liverpool on Sunday, with Burnham pledging to turn the page on a decade of economic and political turmoil.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Hurricane Nolo gains speed as it moves away from Hawaii, but high winds, flash floods are still risk
item.description: Nolo was expected to continue strengthening and turn toward the northwest by Sunday night, though the National Hurricane Center said the center of the storm would remain well south and southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Supreme Court vote shadows Maine Sen. Susan Collins in her first race after abortion rights decision
item.description: The Nov. 3 election will be the first time Collins is on the ballot since the Supreme Court's 2022 ruling that overturned Roe v. Wade, resulting in abortion being banned in much of the United States.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Supreme Court vote shadows Maine Sen. Susan Collins in her first bid after abortion rights decision
item.description: The Nov. 3 election will be the first time Collins is on the ballot since the Supreme Court's 2022 ruling that overturned Roe v. Wade, resulting in abortion being banned in much of the United States.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: UN speakers' go-to quotes: Ancient texts, modern greats and a little Talking Heads
item.description: Speakers this week touched on homeland sayings, ancient texts, figures of moral authority and more — even a bit of Talking Heads (not TV pundits — the 1980s new wave band).

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Swiss reject tighter neutrality rules in referendum backed by right-wing populist party
item.description: Final results from the Swiss government showed 70% of voters, and a majority in all 26 of the country's regions, rejected the plan.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pope blasts assisted dying as 'false compassion' at French shrine known for miraculous cures
item.description: On his third day in France, Leo again waded into the end-of-life debate that has erupted in countries around the world. It roiled French politics for years before resulting recently in legislation allowing adults with incurable illnesses to receive lethal medication.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Eviction of 87-year-old sparks encampment protest in Madrid over housing crisis
item.description: Tens of thousands marched through Madrid on Saturday to protest the eviction of María del Carmen Abascal from the apartment in the upscale Retiro neighborhood where she had lived for more than seven decades.

item.title: NPR: As Congress debates college sports, athletes-turned-senators have a seat at the table
item.description: The Protect College Sports Act is on the brink of passing in the Senate, where a handful of former college athletes who are now senators on both sides of the aisle have an extra say in the debate.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Powerful nor'easter floods Northeast, leaves over 130,000 without power as high tides threaten coast
item.description: The slow-moving storm, which killed a New York City housing authority worker when a tree fell Saturday, was expected to linger through Sunday with heavy rain, strong winds and dangerous surf from New Jersey to New England.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 5 men arrested near air base used by U.S. in Iran war on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act
item.description: Fairford has been used by American bombers for strictly limited strikes against Iran under an agreement with former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who voiced opposition to the war after it was launched by the U.S. and Israel on Feb. 28.

item.title: NPR: As former athletes, some Senators have extra say on the college sports reform bill
item.description: As Senate considers a major college sports reform bill lobbied for by the NCAA and other powerful stakeholders, some lawmakers — themselves former college athletes — have a major say in the debate.

item.title: NPR: Ohio governor's race: Ramaswamy and Acton clash in rare Democratic pickup opportunity
item.description: The Ohio governor's race pits Vivek Ramaswamy against Democrat Amy Acton. While Ramaswamy downplays his Trump tie and Acton faces pandemic-era scrutiny, Democrats eye a rare win in 40 years

item.title: NPR: These Democrats are running for Congress on Christian faith. Will it pay off?
item.description: It's rare for Democrats to make religion a centerpiece of their campaigns. But this midterm election cycle, a number of candidates for Congress are doing just that.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: House Democrats plan vast oversight of Trump administration. Impeachment is an option
item.description: "There is a cost to the American people of the out-of-control corruption," said Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, who is in line to become House speaker if Democrats win control at the Capitol.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Hurricane Nolo expected to unleash powerful winds and flash flooding on Hawaii
item.description: While direct landfall by the storm's center was not expected, forecasters said it could cause life-threatening flooding and mudslides, with parts of the Big Island expected to see rainfall totals up to 20 inches.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Kennedy Center put off planned repairs despite known structural issues, former employees allege
item.description: The center's executive director and chief operating officer, Matt Floca, did not treat the roofing issues as priorities and in April halted a funded plan to address them, according to the letter Thursday signed by David Seide, a lawyer representing the anonymous whistleblowers.

item.title: NPR: Trump calls Iranian plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz not 'acceptable'
item.description: President Trump said he was rejecting an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian proposal is similar to a memorandum of understanding agreed upon by the U.S. and Iran back in June.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: German and Russian foreign ministers have rare meeting at United Nations General Assembly
item.description: In the encounter, German Foreign Minster Johann Wadephul called on Russia to abandon its "dangerous path of escalation" toward Germany, Europe and the NATO alliance, a German delegation official said.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bodies of 6 people, including 4 Americans, recovered from collapsed building in Athens
item.description: The blast on Friday was believed to have been caused by a major gas leak, Athens Mayor Haris Doukas said. Neighboring buildings were damaged and evacuated.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: China and U.S. agree to establish AI safety channel and continue trade and military talks
item.description: The summit produced no major breakthroughs, but analysts said the steps toward greater cooperation were important because they established working groups that could help prevent disputes from escalating.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump administration uses rare authority to claw back nearly $1B in spending approved by Congress
item.description: Most of the cuts are focused on Health and Human Services programs that serve refugees and unaccompanied minors accused of being in the country illegally.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pope Leo draws 800,000 people to central Paris for open-air Mass on iconic square
item.description: The turnout testified to the church's lasting influence in France despite declining attendance and secularizing trends that have emptied churches across Europe.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: CNN says it was left off Air Force One for Trump's Saturday trip to a college football game
item.description: CNN, a member of the U.S. network video pool that rotates duties shooting and sharing video coverage of the president, reported it had been scheduled to fly aboard the president's plane Saturday for a scheduled visit to a college football game.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump rejects Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and other Middle East news
item.description: Iran offered this week to reopen the strait and resume talks on its nuclear program in seven days if the U.S. lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waives sanctions on Iranian oil sales and observes a ceasefire that would include Lebanon.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Roads flood in New Jersey, inundate some homes, as major signs of nor'easter take shape
item.description: Tens of millions of people are in the path of the storm, which was already beginning to lash the region. Dangerous flooding is expected along the Mid-Atlantic coast, particularly near New Jersey and Delaware.

item.title: NPR: Press pool dispute escalates as White House cuts CNN from Air Force One travel
item.description: The White House has barred CNN from traveling on Air Force One this weekend. It's another chapter in President Trump's fight with the press, and it appears there will be no TV pool coverage today.

item.title: NPR: Supreme Court rejects GOP-backed Missouri map, preserving key seat for Democrats
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected a Republican attempt at redistricting congressional seats in Missouri - possibly giving Democrats a boost in their effort to win the House in the midterm elections.

item.title: NPR: Week in Politics: Trump faces Republican defections; U.S.-China summit; press feud
item.description: Some GOP candidates are stepping back from unpopular Trump administration policies. Meanwhile, a U.S.-China summit at the White House and tensions with the press corps.

item.title: NPR: Battle for the Lehigh Valley: Can GOP hold its razor-thin margin?
item.description: Both parties target the Lehigh Valley for House control. While the GOP made inroads with Latinos, Dems argue Trump's immigration stance hurts them. Can Republicans hold this 1% margin swing seat?

item.title: NPR: The U.S. has more thalidomide survivors than the government admits
item.description: In the 1950s and 1960s, doctors gave the drug thalidomide to pregnant patients without telling them — and without FDA approval. Now those patients' children want recognition.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Hacks by autonomous AI agents raise thorny questions of legal accountability
item.description: What happens when the hackers aren't human? That's the question at the center of a public policy debate following disclosures by leading tech companies that their AI models went rogue and hacked into other organizations.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What the Supreme Court's voter-citizenship database decision means for the midterms
item.description: The Supreme Court revived a controversial voter-citizenship database less than two months ahead of the midterm elections. In the ruling, the court sided with the Trump administration, which is seeking to use the Department of Homeland Security's SAVE database to review state voter rolls for potential noncitizens. Geoff Bennett discussed more with Jessica Huseman of Votebeat.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Xi wraps up 3-day state visit with Trump
item.description: In our news wrap Friday, Chinese President Xi wrapped up a three-day state visit with President Trump that was heavy on pageantry and light on policy announcements, tens of millions of people along the East Coast could see flooding, rough surf and high winds due to a powerful nor'easter and New Jersey's lieutenant governor stepped down amid accusations of sexual harassment and ethics violations.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mexico's foreign secretary on Trump, cartel violence and U.S. trade talks
item.description: President Trump struck the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement in his first term, but threw out that trade agreement after retaking office last year. He imposed steep tariffs on both neighbors and even started a trade war with Canada. To discuss trade talks between the countries, Amna Nawaz spoke with Mexico's foreign secretary, Roberto Velasco Álvarez.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Health care costs a major concern for voters ahead of midterms
item.description: Health care is at the center of a political debate as millions of Americans struggle with rising costs. Enrollment in the marketplaces created by the ACA dropped this year, mainly due to the expiration of federal credits. Vice President Vance also announced plans to cancel coverage for nearly 760,000 people, citing claims of widespread fraud. Geoff Bennett discussed with Larry Levitt of KFF.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Supreme Court rejects Trump-backed Missouri congressional map for third time
item.description: The justices halted a federal appeals court ruling that would have revived the Republican-friendly map for the November elections, which will determine control of Congress. There were no noted dissents.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Wrongfully detained Iranian American journalist remains jailed in Iran after 2 years
item.description: This week marks two years that Iranian American journalist Reza Valizadeh has been detained in Iran. For a decade, he worked for Radio Farda — an independent, but U.S.-funded Farsi-language news service. During a trip to Iran to visit family, Valizadeh was arrested and sentenced to ten years in prison for "collaborating with a hostile government." Amna Nawaz spoke with his attorney, Ryan Fayhee.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Violence has displaced more than half a million Mexican households in past 5 years
item.description: Until now, Mexico's government did not share comprehensive data on people who have been forced to flee their homes due to ongoing violence in many parts of Mexico, leaving civil society groups piecing together information to get a wider view of the problem.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: GOP's big bet on Texas Latino voters could backfire in midterms
item.description: Texas Republicans redrew the state's congressional map last year, making a bet that Latino voters who broke for President Trump in 2024 could be the foundation for victory in 2026. But as Liz Landers reports, immigration crackdowns and rising everyday costs in South Texas may be splintering the GOP's new coalition.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Brooks and Capehart on Trump's warm welcome for China's Xi Jinping
item.description: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit, President Trump's warm welcome for the Chinese leader and Trump banning some journalists from the White House.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Syrian dancer reflects on escaping ISIS and finding freedom through ballet
item.description: Ahmad Joudeh is a ballet dancer of unusual grace and grit. He was born stateless in a Palestinian refugee camp in Damascus, Syria. He has traveled far on the power of his dreams and the elegance of his dance. He survived a traumatic childhood, much of Syria's civil war and constant threats of execution by ISIS. We met Joudeh in his new home in San Diego.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: More than 167,000 pounds of meat were recalled. What to know about the state of food safety in the U.S.
item.description: More than 167,000 pounds of beef, pork and goat meat are being recalled after they were produced without the required federal inspection and labeled with a false inspection sticker, according to the Department of Agriculture.

item.title: NPR: Supreme Court blocks Trump-backed Missouri congressional map
item.description: The ruling is a defeat for Republicans seeking to give their party an edge in the midterm elections for control of the House. It means voters will face a different map than the one used in the primary elections.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump promised to campaign in midterm battlegrounds. He's starting in deep red states instead
item.description: While organizers insist the rallies are in locations with media markets that span state lines and they will help bolster broader turnout, Trump's itinerary is yet another sign of the uphill fight that his party faces.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mississippi police say Tasia Fortune's hanging was 'staged' after her death in a drug dispute
item.description: Authorities haven't disclosed the exact cause of Fortune's death, but they did rule it a homicide and have arrested two men, both of them Black, on murder charges. They also issued an arrest warrant for a third, unnamed, person.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New Jersey's lieutenant governor resigns after sexual harassment and ethics complaints
item.description: Gov. Mikie Sherrill had given Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell until Friday to bring an end to a scandal that threatened to be a drag on her fledgling administration.

item.title: NPR: What did we learn from the Trump-Xi summit?
item.description: President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping wrap up their two-day summit. What did we learn beyond the pageantry?

item.title: NPR: Takeaways from the Trump-Xi state visit: Pageantry and pandas
item.description: The visit comes at an important time for both men.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Report finds many security deficiencies at Utah university where Charlie Kirk was killed
item.description: A new report on Charlie Kirk's assassination last year says his Turning Point USA organization insisted he speak outdoors despite security concerns, while the university where he was killed didn't properly assess dangers like the possibility of a rooftop shooter.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Hurricane Nolo threatening Hawaii with heavy rain as Polo churns near Mexico
item.description: Residents on Hawaii's Big Island were bracing Friday for potentially life-threatening and catastrophic flooding from Hurricane Nolo, while Mexico was still under the threat of Hurricane Polo as it headed toward the Baja Peninsula after bringing storm conditions to the southwestern coast.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New Mexico jury finds Facebook liable of deceiving users about privacy protections
item.description: The trial centered on accusations that Facebook deceived users about a data breach stemming from a third-party personality quiz that harvested data from roughly 87 million profiles and sold it to a political consulting firm, Cambridge Analytica, to generate targeted ads.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Nor'easter to lash the East Coast with strong winds, flooding and heavy rain
item.description: Millions of people were under warnings associated with the storm, which has already cancelled concerts and prompted people on islands near Cape Cod to head to the mainland in the days ahead of the nor'easter's arrival.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pope Leo XIV affirms need for media to cover public figures when asked about Trump ban
item.description: Pope Leo XIV told journalists they were welcome to report on him, as he responded to the Trump administration's attempt to bar U.S. media from the White House and affirmed the importance of journalists covering public figures.

item.title: NPR: The Supreme Court revives a controversial data system for citizenship checks
item.description: The Supreme Court is allowing use of a data system that Trump officials overhauled. The system has erroneously flagged U.S. citizens and a lower court found it violated federal privacy protections.

item.title: NPR: Trump and China's Xi discuss AI, trade and Iran war during state visit
item.description: U.S. President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met for the second time this year to much fanfare but little in the way of grand bargains.

item.title: NPR: Americans are confused and worried about elections. Will that impact turnout?
item.description: New polling shows many voters are concerned about the midterms. But prior elections show no clear link between voter concerns and fewer voters actually casting ballots.

item.title: NPR: As election enters its final stretch, some Republicans are distancing from Trump
item.description: With less than six weeks until Election Day, a growing number of Republicans are breaking from Trump on key issues. It comes as the party is scrambling to hold onto a slim majority in Congress.

item.title: NPR: Congress passed $100 million for teen pregnancy prevention. Most of it is untouched
item.description: With days left to go in the 2026 fiscal year, lawmakers push the health department to spend the money Congress allocated to prevent teen pregnancy. An NPR exclusive.

item.title: NPR: Trump's state dinner for Xi features sea bass and a long list of tech titans
item.description: A tech-heavy guest list, the fashion choices of those on it, who sat where and what was on the menu marked the softer — often and glitzier — details of diplomacy as Donald Trump threw a Thursday night state dinner honoring China's leader Xi Jinping.

item.title: NPR: Long agenda, short meeting: Trump and Xi meet
item.description: All Things Considered host Mary Louise Kelly talks with White House correspondent Emily Feng about the Trump/Xi summit.
